key_insight: A ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 D-gun coating substantially improves the tribological wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and a random forest model best predicts wear from test conditions.
engineering_relevance: This shows detonation-sprayed ceramic coatings can extend titanium alloy life in aerospace, biomedical, and marine sliding components while machine learning helps optimize wear performance.
method: Applied Al2O3-TiO2 coating to Ti-6Al-4V by detonation gun under controlled spray conditions.
Ran pin-on-disc wear tests per ASTM G99 over 40–100 N, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min against EN31 steel.
Built ANN, KNN, and random forest models to predict wear from sliding parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced wear and tribo-layer formation on coated surfaces, with random forest giving the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: The findings are based on a limited experimental range and require validation before use on different geometries, environments, or service loads.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
